title: MiniRiskers FCRM risk decomposition — supervisory framework mapping
description: Maps every risk category, risk factor and concentration rule used by the MiniRiskers risk model to the published supervisory frameworks it is derived from. Indian clauses were checked against the regulatory texts in Documents/ (paragraph numbers as printed in those copies). International frameworks are cited at the level of the recommendation or document section, not invented paragraph numbers.

methodology_basis.principle: Risk assessment is decomposed into customer, geography, product/service/transaction and delivery-channel risk.

references.requirement: REs shall carry out an ML/TF risk assessment to identify, assess and mitigate risk for clients, countries or geographic areas, products, services, transactions or delivery channels.
Identify, assess and understand ML/TF risks and apply a risk-based approach.

references.clause: Section on risk assessment — risk categories
references.requirement: Country/geographic, customer, product/service/transaction and delivery-channel risk as the core risk categories.

methodology_basis.principle: New products, business practices and technologies are risk-assessed before launch.

references.requirement: Undertake ML/TF risk assessments prior to the launch or use of new products, practices, services and technologies, and manage the risk with EDD and transaction monitoring.
Assess risks of new products, business practices, delivery mechanisms and technologies prior to launch.
Risk assessments of digital payment products both prior to establishing the service and regularly thereafter.

methodology_basis.principle: Inherent risk is assessed first, controls are then evaluated, and the result is residual risk. Controls mitigate risk but never eliminate it.

references.clause: FAQ — inherent risk, control effectiveness and residual risk
references.requirement: Assess inherent risk across risk categories, assess the design and operating effectiveness of controls, and derive residual risk.

references.clause: Assessment, understanding, management and mitigation of risks
references.requirement: Banks should understand their inherent risk and apply mitigating controls proportionate to it.
Consider all relevant risk factors before determining the overall risk level and the appropriate level and type of mitigation; document the assessment.

methodology_basis.principle: Customers and relationships are rated on a Low / Medium / High scale using documented parameters.

references.requirement: Customers shall be categorised as low, medium and high risk, based on documented parameters.

CUSTOMER.label: Customer
CUSTOMER.definition: Risk arising from who the customers are: type, status (e.g. PEP), onboarding method and population size.

references.requirement: Client risk as a mandatory dimension; risk categorisation of customers.
CDD measures scaled to customer risk.
Identify and verify clients and beneficial owners.
Customer type and characteristics as an inherent risk category.

PRODUCT.label: Product
PRODUCT.definition: Risk from the product or service itself: novelty, cross-border reach and digital delivery.

references.requirement: Products and services as a risk dimension; pre-launch assessment of new products.
Assess risks of new products and business practices.
Product features that increase anonymity, speed or cross-border reach raise risk.

GEOGRAPHY.label: Geography
GEOGRAPHY.definition: Risk from the countries involved: cross-border exposure, high-risk jurisdictions and sanctions.

references.requirement: Geographic risk dimension; EDD for jurisdictions that do not or insufficiently apply FATF Recommendations.
Enhanced due diligence for business with higher-risk countries.
Freezing and prohibition obligations for designated individuals and entities.
Country risk as an inherent risk category.

TRANSACTION.label: Transaction
TRANSACTION.definition: Risk from how money moves: velocity, cross-border flows, round amounts and rapid movement.

references.requirement: Monitor large, complex and unusual transactions and high turnover; align monitoring with risk category.
Record prescribed cash, cross-border and suspicious transactions.
Maintain records of transactions and furnish information to FIU-IND.

references.clause: Recommendation 16 (Wire transfers); Recommendation 20 (Reporting of suspicious transactions)
references.requirement: Originator/beneficiary information on transfers and STR reporting.

CHANNEL.label: Delivery channel
CHANNEL.definition: Risk from how the product reaches customers: mobile, remote onboarding and third-party channels.

references.requirement: Delivery-channel risk dimension; enhanced measures for non-face-to-face onboarding.

references.clause: Chapter II (General controls); Chapter IV (Mobile payments application security)
references.requirement: Governance and security controls for internet and mobile payment channels.
Non-face-to-face and intermediated channels as risk drivers.

THIRD_PARTY.label: Third party
THIRD_PARTY.definition: Risk introduced by vendors and service providers that process transactions or data, including cross-border processing.

references.clause: Para 13 (Due diligence on service providers); Para 17 (Risk management framework); Para 21 (Cross-border outsourcing)
references.requirement: Due diligence, risk management and additional controls for outsourced and cross-border IT services.
Reliance on third parties does not transfer ultimate responsibility for CDD.
Ultimate responsibility for CDD remains with the financial institution.
Oversight and controls where digital payment services depend on third-party providers.

FRAUD.label: Fraud
FRAUD.definition: Risk that the product is used to commit or launder the proceeds of fraud (e.g. mule accounts, rapid pass-through).

references.clause: Section 2.1 (Fraud risk management policy); Section 3 (Early Warning Signals and Red Flagging)
references.requirement: Board-approved fraud risk management and early detection of frauds.

references.clause: Para 59 (Operation of bank accounts & money mules)
references.requirement: Monitoring to identify money-mule accounts used to launder fraud proceeds.
Risk assessment of digital payment products, including fraud exposure.

PRODUCT:New Product.requirement: Pre-launch ML/TF risk assessment of new products and practices.
New products and technologies are assessed before launch.

PRODUCT:Cross Border Product.requirement: Information requirements for cross-border wire transfers.

PRODUCT:Digital Product Channel.requirement: Policy, governance, product-level risk limits and risk assessment for digital payment products.
New delivery mechanisms and technologies are risk-assessed.

CUSTOMER:PEP Exposure.requirement: Risk management systems, senior management approval and enhanced monitoring for PEPs.
Enhanced measures for politically exposed persons.

CUSTOMER:High Risk Customer Exposure.requirement: High-risk categorisation, periodic review and EDD.

CUSTOMER:Digital Onboarding.requirement: Controls for video-based and non-face-to-face customer identification.
CDD reliability for non-face-to-face and technology-enabled onboarding.

CUSTOMER:Large Customer Population.requirement: Risk assessment proportionate to the nature, size and complexity of activities.
Customer volumes as an inherent risk driver.

GEOGRAPHY:Cross Border Geography.requirement: Geographic risk and cross-border wire-transfer requirements.

GEOGRAPHY:High Risk Jurisdiction.requirement: EDD for jurisdictions in FATF statements or insufficiently applying FATF Recommendations.
Enhanced due diligence and countermeasures for higher-risk countries.

GEOGRAPHY:Sanctions Exposure.requirement: Freeze and report funds of designated individuals and entities.

GEOGRAPHY:Sanctions Exposure.clause: Paras 51-53 (UAPA and WMD obligations; UNSCR sanctions lists)
GEOGRAPHY:Sanctions Exposure.requirement: Screen against UN and domestic designated lists.
Freeze without delay the assets of designated persons.

TRANSACTION:Cross Border Transactions.requirement: Records of prescribed cross-border wire transfers.
Originator and beneficiary information for cross-border transfers.

TRANSACTION:High Transaction Velocity.requirement: Monitor high account turnover inconsistent with the balance maintained.

TRANSACTION:Round Amount Pattern.requirement: Monitor transactions with unusual patterns and no apparent economic rationale.
Unusual transaction patterns as suspicious-transaction indicators.

TRANSACTION:Rapid Movement.requirement: Monitor unusual patterns and deposits followed by large withdrawals.
Record and report suspicious transactions to FIU-IND.

CHANNEL:Mobile Banking.clause: Chapter IV (Mobile payments application security controls)
CHANNEL:Mobile Banking.requirement: Security controls for mobile payment applications.

CHANNEL:Remote Onboarding.requirement: Controls for remote and non-face-to-face onboarding.

CHANNEL:Third Party Channel.requirement: Reliance on third parties for CDD keeps ultimate responsibility with the RE.
Reliance on third parties and intermediaries.

THIRD_PARTY:Third Party Transaction Proc.clause: Para 13; Para 17; Para 19 (Monitoring and control of outsourced activities)
THIRD_PARTY:Third Party Transaction Proc.requirement: Due diligence, risk management and ongoing monitoring of service providers.

THIRD_PARTY:Customer Data Handling.clause: Para 16 (Aspects to be considered in agreement)
THIRD_PARTY:Customer Data Handling.requirement: Contractual confidentiality, security and audit rights over customer data.
Protection of customer information across the IT estate.

THIRD_PARTY:Payment Data Handling.requirement: Oversight of third-party providers in the digital payment ecosystem.
Risk management framework for outsourced services.

THIRD_PARTY:Cross Border Processing.requirement: Country risk, legal enforceability and regulator access for cross-border service providers.

FRAUD:High Transaction Velocity.requirement: Early warning signals for early detection of frauds.

FRAUD:Rapid Movement Pattern.requirement: Identify accounts used to launder the proceeds of fraud.
Fraud risk management policy and governance.

cross-border-velocity.requirement: Speed combined with cross-border reach compounds ML/TF risk.
Enhanced monitoring of unusual high-turnover cross-border activity.

pep-high-risk-customer.requirement: PEP relationships need senior management approval and enhanced monitoring.

sanctions-exposure.requirement: Sanctions obligations are absolute and cannot be offset by other controls.
Targeted financial sanctions apply without delay.
